newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disappointed by EU move over Cuba law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disappointed by EU move over Cuba law.

text.p: The United States has said it was disappointed the European Union had only delayed and not dropped moves to have the World Trade Organisation rule on complaints that a U.S. anti-Cuba law violates trade rules.

European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said Wednesday he had asked WTO chief Renato Ruggiero to delay naming a panel to make the ruling until Feb. 20 in a bid to reach a settlement with Washington over the Helms-Burton Act.

"It's helpful that they've decided to postpone the question, but we're a little bit disappointed they've only postponed and not dropped or suspended entirely this request," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns on Thursday.

"We've said many times that ... Helms-Burton is first and foremost a law of the land. It's also a foreign policy matter. We don't consider it to be a trade issue. We consider it to be a foreign policy issue," Burns told a news briefing.

The EU and the United States have been at odds for nearly a year over the act, which penalises foreign companies that benefit from investments in property confiscated from U.S. citizens by Havana since the 1959 communist revolution.
The two sides have been unable to agree the composition of the panel and last week Brittan called for Ruggiero to intervene.

Burns said Washington believed it was "inappropriate for the WTO to consider this issue at all ... It's a highly political matter, and we think it will just have adverse implications for the way that the WTO does business."
